leverage.exposure: No leverage, in any branch. Every live bid plus the one being recommended still totals comfortably less than the cash on hand, so a negative balance cannot open at matchday start and the zero-score risk is not in play. The spending floor is nowhere near binding either; cash is the constraint that matters, and it clears. The exposure that does matter is structural rather than financial: at ten players the hundred-point penalty is live right now, and a single defender landing this morning ends it. The second-order risk is the one worth watching — if the transfer completes and the squad loses a forward involuntarily after the window has shut, the remaining shape fills no formation, which is the same penalty arriving by a different door. The body being bought today covers both doors.

binding_gap: The binding gap is one outfield body, and specifically a midfielder or a forward rather than another defender. The eleven caps defenders at five, so a sixth and seventh defender add depth but cannot widen the shape; with only two midfielders on the books, every legal formation runs through the same narrow configuration. That is why the buy this run is a midfielder despite two defender auctions already being live, and why the goalkeepers that keep appearing at floor prices — four of them in the last two days — must keep being refused however cheap they look.

verdict.headline: Deadline day.
verdict.detail: Deadline day. A dated story published this morning has Club Brugge making a concrete approach for Sylla before the German window shuts at 18:00Z, and that turns a slow squad-building run into a timed one. The exposure is not that Georg loses a good player — Sylla scores almost nothing — it is that if Kickbase deletes him from the squad the shape collapses into a formation that cannot be filled, and the -100 arrives without Georg touching anything. The whole plan today is to buy one cheap outfield body that resolves BEFORE the deadline, so the Sylla sale becomes legal and the deletion risk is insured at the same time. Everything else holds.

sell.reason: Sylla is the sale, and it is a race against the window rather than a value judgement. He starts, he is fit, and he contributes twenty-one points to the best eleven — losing him costs almost nothing on the pitch. What makes it urgent is the shape: a squad that loses him involuntarily, after the window, cannot field a legal eleven. But the sale is gated, and the gate must not be forced. At twelve players in the current shape, selling him leaves a side that fills no formation at all, which would be self-inflicted. The sale only becomes legal once a third midfielder has landed. If that body is lost at auction, the right answer is to let the risk ride into the Belgian window rather than sell into an illegal shape. Widmer remains the designated funding sale afterwards — benched, bleeding value daily, and outside the best eleven either way, so selling him costs nothing in points. Bernardo would take his place in that queue only if the Kickbase fitness flag on him is still showing near the lock; the dated club and injury sources currently say he is fit, so the flag reads as the hook he suffered rather than a knock.

Window shuts 20:00 CET = 2026-09-01T18:00Z. THE COST OF SELLING IS 21 ap AND NOTHING ELSE: at 13 = 1/6/3/3 the best XI is 5-2-3 for 1442 ap with Sylla; after the sale, 12 = 1/6/3/2 fields 5-3-2 for 1421 ap. THE DELETION RISK IS THE REAL POINT: if the move completes, Kickbase removes him and compensates at mv, dropping a 12-man squad to 11 = 1GK/6DEF/2MID/2ATT, which fills NO formation because DEF caps at 5 - that is a -100 on MD2 arriving without Georg touching anything. If Amoako is lost at ~10:45Z the sale simply cannot happen today and the risk rides into the Belgian window - accept that rather than selling into an illegal shape. SEQUENCE: 09:23Z ter Horst resolves, ~10:45Z Amoako, 11:52Z Maluze, then recount and sell before 18:00Z.

buy.reason: One buy, and it reverses a call this ledger made yesterday — Amoako, previously avoided as an overpriced cheap body, is now the recommendation. The reversal is on timing, not on value, and the earlier reasoning was never wrong about the value. He is the only fit outfield player on the board whose auction resolves before the transfer deadline. Everything else available before then is either a goalkeeper, which is structurally useless because only one can ever be fielded, or injured, or costs several million more for points that never reach the eleven — the second midfield slot is already occupied, so the expensive midfielders on the board add literally nothing to the best side. He is a bench body with no starts, and that is stated plainly rather than dressed up; what is being bought is a legal shape, not a scorer. He is not the trap that caught two other clean-looking listings this week, because he has actually been named in matchday squads, which means a fitness flag would have shown if there were one. The bid is deliberately set deep into the premium band measured for cheap contested listings, because bidding the middle of that band is precisely how the last three of these were lost. The purchase is robust whichever way the two defender auctions fall: it either unlocks the sale or, in the worst branch, ends the penalty outright on its own.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. There are no manager asks sitting below market value, so the mechanism the value trade depends on is simply absent. The rivals continue to trade injured and unavailable players against each other for fractions of a percent on the daily tick, and one of them this morning demonstrated exactly why that is not a model worth copying: a body bought yesterday at a record premium was dumped back to Kickbase at flat market value overnight for a substantial loss, in under fifteen hours. The lesson worth keeping is that these premiums are winnable but never recoverable on resale — so they should only ever be paid for a body that is genuinely needed, which is the case being made for today's buy and was not the case for his.

fitness.sweep: A squad-wide sweep of the injury and suspension table returns nothing: no player in the squad, and none of the three players Georg is bidding on, appears on it. Bernardo still carries a fitness flag inside Kickbase, but the dated club sources say he returned to the squad before the last matchday and started it, so the flag most likely reflects being substituted early rather than an injury — worth re-checking closer to the lock, since he is the fifth defender and would actually be fielded. Two date traps were cleared this run, both of which a future run will meet again. The widely-circulated headline announcing that Sylla is leaving Schalke is from January and concerns a completely different, collapsed move to a club in the United States; it does not corroborate the current story. And the club statement listing him as injured for a fixture against Bayern belongs to last season's calendar, not this one.
